title: Ginger beef and broccoli stir-fry
blurb: Tender beef strips and crisp broccoli in a glossy ginger and oyster sauce, served over fluffy jasmine rice.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: bring to the boil, cover, turn the heat right down and cook for 12 minutes. Leave covered off the heat.
Toss the beef with the {cornflour}, half the soy sauce and the black pepper. In a small bowl, stir the oyster sauce with the rest of the soy and {ml 60} of water.
Heat half the oil in a wok over a high heat. Fry the beef for 2 minutes until browned, then tip it onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the broccoli with the {spring onion} whites for 3 minutes, adding a splash of water to steam it slightly.
Add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and return the beef. Bubble for 1 minute until glossy.
Serve over the rice, scattered with the {spring onion} greens.

title: Sweet and sour chicken with peppers
blurb: Crisp-edged chicken, pineapple and peppers tossed in a bright, tangy sauce you can balance to taste.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce the heat to its lowest and cook for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat.
Stir the ketchup, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and 4 tbsp of the pineapple juice or water together for the sauce.
Toss the chicken in {10 g|1 tbsp} of the {cornflour} and the salt. Fry it in half the oil over a medium-high heat for 6 to 7 minutes until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion and peppers for 4 minutes so they keep some bite.
Return the chicken, add the pineapple and pour in the sauce. Mix the remaining {cornflour} with 1 tbsp of water, stir it in and bubble for 1 minute until thick and glossy.
Spoon over the rice and serve.

title: Fiery mapo-style tofu with mushrooms
blurb: Silky tofu and savoury mushrooms in a numbing-hot, {chilli}-oil sauce. Properly spicy and very vegan.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, turn right down and cook for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat.
Cover the tofu cubes with boiling water and the salt and leave for 5 minutes to firm up, then drain gently.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat. Fry the mushrooms for 5 minutes until deeply browned and dry.
Add the garlic, ginger, {spring onion} whites, {chilli flakes} and the {chilli} oil, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the soy sauce, sugar, black pepper and {ml 200} of water. Slide in the tofu and simmer for 4 minutes.
Mix the {cornflour} with 2 tbsp of cold water, stir it in and cook for 1 minute until the sauce clings. Serve over the rice with the {spring onion} greens.

title: Egg fried rice with peas and {spring onion}
blurb: Fast, satisfying fried rice with soft scrambled egg, sweet peas and toasted sesame oil.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the salt. Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok over a high heat and scramble the eggs for 30 seconds until just set, then tip them out.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the carrot and {spring onion} whites for 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and rice, pressing it against the hot wok and tossing for 3 minutes until it begins to crisp.
Stir in the peas, soy sauce and pepper and cook for 2 minutes. Fold the egg back in.
Finish with the sesame oil and the {spring onion} greens.

title: Hoisin pork and {pak choi} noodles
blurb: Sticky hoisin pork strips with wilted {pak choi} and slippery egg noodles, a gentle-heat midweek favourite.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water to the packet time, drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the hoisin, soy sauce, rice vinegar and 3 tbsp of water in a small bowl.
Heat half the oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the pork for 3 to 4 minutes until browned at the edges, then remove.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the carrot and {pak choi} stems for 2 minutes, then add the ginger, garlic and half the {chilli} for 30 seconds.
Return the pork with the noodles, {pak choi} leaves and sauce. Toss for 2 minutes until everything is hot and coated.
Serve topped with the remaining {chilli}.

title: Chicken katsu curry with rice
blurb: Crunchy panko chicken with a mild, sweet Japanese-style curry sauce and a quick cucumber pickle.

ingredients.prep: sliced in half horizontally to make 2 thin cutlets

steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat. Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Soften the onion and carrot in 1 tbsp of the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, {20 g|2½ tbsp} of the flour and the curry powder and stir for 1 minute.
Crumble in the {stock cube}, add {ml 350} of water, the soy sauce and the sugar. Simmer for 12 minutes, then blend with a stick blender until smooth, or leave chunky if you prefer.
Season the chicken with salt. Coat each piece in the remaining flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on {kitchen paper}.
Slice the chicken and serve over the rice with the curry sauce and cucumber pickle.

title: Teriyaki salmon and edamame rice bowl
blurb: Glazed salmon over sticky rice with edamame and crunchy cucumber. Ready in just over twenty minutes.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat. Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger together until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the salmon for 3 minutes on one side until golden.
Turn the fillets, pour in the teriyaki mixture and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning it over until sticky and the fish is just cooked.
Divide the rice between bowls and add the edamame and cucumber. Flake or slice the salmon on top, drizzle with the pan glaze and scatter over the {spring onion} and sesame seeds.

title: Miso-glazed {aubergine} rice bowl
blurb: Sweet-salty miso {aubergine} roasted until soft and caramelised, with rice, cucumber and sesame.

ingredients.prep: halved lengthways, flesh scored in a criss-cross

steps: Heat the oven to {oven 220}. Brush the cut sides of the {aubergine} with 2 tbsp of the oil and roast cut-side down on a tray for 20 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest off the heat.
Whisk the miso, mirin, soy sauce and sugar with 1 tbsp of water until smooth.
Turn the {aubergine} cut-side up, spread the miso glaze over the flesh and roast for 8 to 10 minutes more until sticky and bubbling at the edges.
Serve the {aubergine} on the rice with the cucumber, {spring onion} and sesame seeds.

title: Miso tofu and mushroom udon broth
blurb: A light, savoury miso broth with chunky udon, golden tofu, mushrooms and {pak choi}.
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 5 minutes, turning until golden on most sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the mushrooms and ginger for 4 minutes until lightly browned.
Add {ml 700} of water, the crumbled {stock cube}, soy sauce and mirin and bring to a simmer.
Add the udon and {pak choi} and simmer for 3 minutes until the noodles are loose and hot.
Ladle a little broth into a cup, whisk in the miso until smooth and stir it back into the pan. Do not boil it again.
Divide into bowls, top with the tofu and {spring onion} and finish with the sesame oil.

title: Gochujang pork rice bowl
blurb: Sticky, spicy {pork mince|ground pork} over rice with quick-pickled cucumber and crunchy carrot.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar and a pinch of the sugar and leave to pickle.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and fry the pork, breaking it up, for 6 minutes until browned and any liquid has cooked off.
Add the garlic, ginger and half the {spring onion} for 1 minute, then stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar and 3 tbsp of water. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until sticky.
Spoon the pork over the rice with the cucumber and carrot. Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter over the sesame seeds and remaining {spring onion}.

title: Veggie bibimbap with a fried egg
blurb: Rice topped with sesame spinach, carrots, mushrooms and a runny egg, finished with gochujang sauce.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Stir the gochujang, sugar, 1 tsp of the sesame oil and 2 tbsp of water into a sauce.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan for 1 minute, squeeze out the water and toss with 1 tsp of soy sauce, a little sesame oil, the garlic and the salt.
Fry the carrot in 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil for 3 minutes, then remove. Fry the mushrooms in the same pan with the remaining soy sauce for 5 minutes until golden.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil over a medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are crisp and the yolks runny.
Divide the rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables and cucumber on top and add an egg. Drizzle with the remaining sesame oil, scatter with sesame seeds and serve with the sauce to stir through.

title: Kimchi and crispy tofu fried rice
blurb: Tangy kimchi, golden tofu and gochujang-spiced rice in one wok. Hot, funky and fully vegan.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then spread out on a tray to cool and dry.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the tofu for 6 to 7 minutes, tossing until crisp and golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, the {spring onion} whites, garlic and half the {chilli} and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the kimchi and cook for 2 minutes, then add the gochujang and rice, tossing and pressing for 4 minutes until hot and lightly crisp.
Stir in the soy sauce and return the tofu. Serve with the sesame oil, sesame seeds, {spring onion} greens and remaining {chilli}.

title: Bulgogi-style beef rice bowl
blurb: Sweet, garlicky marinated beef seared hot and piled over rice with crisp lettuce and cucumber.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, half the sesame oil, garlic, ginger and grated apple in a bowl. Add the beef and marinate for at least 10 minutes while you cook the rice.
Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan until very hot. Fry the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each, until caramelised at the edges.
Return all the beef with any marinade left in the bowl and bubble for 30 seconds.
Serve over the rice with lettuce leaves and cucumber, scattered with the {spring onion} and sesame seeds and drizzled with the remaining sesame oil.

title: Thai green chicken curry with green beans
blurb: Creamy coconut green curry with tender chicken thigh, {courgette} and green beans, finished with lime.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the green beans and {courgette} and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Squeeze in the juice of half the lime, taste and adjust. Serve with the rice, {coriander} and a wedge of the remaining lime.

title: Thai red sweet potato and spinach curry
blurb: Sweet potato and {red pepper} simmered in a fragrant coconut and red curry sauce with wilted spinach.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato and {red pepper}, stir to coat, then pour in the coconut milk, {ml 100} of water, the soy sauce and the sugar.
Simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes until the sweet potato is soft but holding its shape.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then squeeze in half the lime juice. Serve with the rice, {coriander} and a lime wedge.

title: {Prawn} pad Thai with lime and peanuts
blurb: Wok-fried rice noodles with {king prawns}, egg and bean sprouts in a sweet-sour-salty sauce.
steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes until pliable but firm, then drain.
Stir the fish sauce, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and sriracha together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat half the oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the {prawns} for 2 minutes until pink, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and {spring onion} for 20 seconds. Push to one side, crack in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce is absorbed. Return the {prawns}, add the bean sprouts and toss for 1 minute.
Serve scattered with the peanuts and a lime wedge to squeeze over.

title: Thai-style pork with {chilli}, basil and green beans
blurb: A hot, salty-sweet pork stir-fry with plenty of {chilli} and basil, served over jasmine rice.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp of water together.
Heat the oil in a wok over a high heat. Add the {chilli} and garlic and stir for 15 seconds, then add the pork, breaking it up, and fry for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the green beans and sauce and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the beans are just tender and the sauce has reduced.
Take off the heat and stir through most of the basil. Serve over the rice with the remaining basil.

title: Peanut tofu and rice noodle bowl
blurb: Crisp tofu and crunchy vegetables with rice noodles in a creamy peanut, lime and {chilli} dressing.

ingredients.prep: cut into cubes and patted dry

steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes until tender, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, juice of the lime, sriracha, ginger, garlic and 4 tbsp of warm water into a smooth dressing.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Toss the noodles with the carrot, {red pepper} and most of the dressing.
Divide into bowls and top with the tofu, drizzle with the remaining dressing and scatter over the {coriander} and peanuts.

title: Lemongrass chicken noodle bowl
blurb: Fragrant lemongrass chicken over cool rice noodles, crunchy veg and herbs with a sharp lime dressing.
steps: Mix the lemongrass, half the garlic, {ml 10} of the fish sauce and {5 g|1 tsp} of the sugar through the chicken and leave to marinate while you prepare everything else.
Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Make the dressing by stirring the remaining fish sauce, garlic and sugar with the juice of 1.5 limes, the {chilli} and 3 tbsp of water.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and fry the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes until caramelised and cooked through.
Divide the noodles into bowls and top with the cucumber, carrot, herbs and chicken. Pour over the dressing and scatter with the peanuts and a wedge of the remaining lime.

title: Caramel ginger salmon with {pak choi}
blurb: Salmon glazed in a sticky caramel, ginger and fish sauce with steamed {pak choi} and rice.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.

Melt the sugar with 1 tbsp of water in a small pan over a medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until amber. Carefully add the fish sauce, 3 tbsp of water, the ginger, garlic and pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat and sear the salmon for 3 minutes per side.
Pour in the caramel and spoon it over the fish for 1 to 2 minutes until sticky.
Meanwhile steam the {pak choi} in a covered pan with a splash of water for 3 minutes.
Serve the salmon over the rice with the {pak choi}, {chilli}, {spring onion} and a squeeze of lime.

title: Crispy tofu and herb noodle salad
blurb: Cool rice noodles with golden tofu, mint, {coriander} and a sweet-sharp lime and {chilli} dressing.

ingredients.prep: cut into cubes and patted dry

steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Stir the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, half the {chilli} and the juice of 1.5 limes with 3 tbsp of water until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp on all sides. Toss with 1 tbsp of the dressing.
Toss the noodles with the cucumber, carrot, mint and {coriander}.
Divide into bowls, top with the tofu, pour over the remaining dressing and finish with the peanuts, remaining {chilli} and a lime wedge.

title: Chicken satay with coconut rice and cucumber
blurb: Peanut-marinated chicken pan-grilled until charred, served with a warm satay sauce and cooling cucumber.
steps: Mix the chicken with half the soy sauce, half the garlic, the ginger and {10 g|2 tsp} of the peanut butter. Marinate for 10 minutes.
Rinse the rice and cook it in a lidded pan with the coconut milk and {ml 150} of water: bring to the boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes and rest off the heat.
For the sauce, warm the remaining peanut butter, soy sauce, garlic and sweet {chilli} sauce in a small pan with {ml 100} of water and the juice of half the lime, stirring until smooth and glossy.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and fry the chicken for 7 to 8 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve the chicken on the rice with the cucumber and {coriander}, the sauce spooned over and the remaining lime in wedges.

title: Vegetable nasi goreng with a fried egg
blurb: Sweet, smoky and spicy Indonesian fried rice with peas and carrots, topped with a crisp-edged egg.
steps: Cook the rice in a lidded pan with {ml 300} of water: boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then spread on a tray to cool for a few minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, sriracha and sugar with 1 tbsp of water.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok over a medium-high heat. Fry the shallots, garlic and {chilli} for 2 minutes, then add the carrot for 2 minutes more.
Add the rice and toss for 3 minutes, then add the peas and sauce and stir-fry for 2 minutes until sticky and hot.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a small pan until the whites are crisp and the yolks runny.
Serve the rice topped with the eggs, with the cucumber and {spring onion} on the side.

title: Gado-gado with crispy tofu and peanut sauce
blurb: Warm potatoes, green beans, cabbage and bean sprouts under crispy tofu and a thick, lime-bright peanut sauce.

ingredients.prep: cut into cubes and patted dry

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 to 14 minutes until tender. Add the green beans for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sweet {chilli} sauce, garlic, {chilli}, the juice of the lime and {ml 100} of warm water until smooth and pourable.
Pour boiling water over the cabbage and bean sprouts in a bowl, leave for 30 seconds, then drain well so they stay crunchy but lose their raw edge.
Arrange the potatoes, beans, cabbage, bean sprouts and cucumber on plates, top with the tofu and pour over the peanut sauce.
